hero.title: Globally Supported Linux,
hero.subtitle: A reliable global Linux OS built for every region and language.

builtForYou.title: Built for you.
builtForYou.description: Oreon provides a high-performance operating system designed with the user at the core. It is built for many people, from basic users to developers.

carousel.familiarWorkflowDesc: A familiar, beautiful desktop environment designed to avoid relearning the ropes of a new OS.
carousel.optimizedPerformanceDesc: With a wide range of hardware support, Oreon ensures it is fully dedicated to your workload without older devices being left behind.
carousel.absolutePrivacyDesc: Oreon will never steal your data. No telemetry, no tracking. It is built for sensitive professional environments where digital privacy is mandatory.

gnome.title: The GNOME Experience
gnome.intro: Oreon is built on GNOME. This provides a mature, easy to use, and highly customizable desktop environment that gets the job done.
gnome.trustedTechnologyDesc: GNOME is a mature, easy to use, and fairly customizable desktop environment developed by Red Hat and the FOSS community.
gnome.communityDrivenDesc: GNOME is a community-driven desktop environment that is free and open source. We recommend donating to GNOME to support their hard work.

globalSupport.title: Global Support Effort
globalSupport.p1: Oreon is designed to be accessible wherever it is used. The operating system supports a wide range of languages natively, and we are expanding translated documentation and community resources to make Oreon easier to use everywhere.
globalSupport.p2: Our goal is simple. No region should feel like a secondary audience. Whether someone is installing Oreon at home or deploying it in a business setting, they should be able to do so in their preferred language with clear documentation and reliable guidance.
globalSupport.p3: Global support for us means more than just translation. It means a commitment to making our community and resources available beyond English. We are building the infrastructure to support contributors around the world so that Oreon grows with its global community, not just for it.
globalSupport.p4: This is a long-term commitment. Oreon is built to serve users and organizations wherever they are.

privacy.title: Your data is your property.
privacy.p1: Oreon is built from the ground up to respect digital privacy. We will never steal your data, track your usage, or force cloud-based telemetry into your OS.
privacy.p2: Every connection is transparent, every background task is auditable. This makes Oreon the perfect OS for users who value their privacy.

community.title: Oreon is community-driven.
community.p: Oreon is community-driven. We promise to publish open source code and support upstream communities to keep Oreon open for everyone.

about.title: Our Community
about.subtitle: Oreon is built by people who are involved in the Linux/FOSS community.
about.whatWeBelieveDesc: This is how we build Oreon and work with the rest of FOSS.
about.openByDefaultDesc: Code is public. You can fork it, read it, or contribute.
about.upstreamLoveDesc: We send changes back to upstream projects when we can.
about.supportTimelinesDesc: We are clear about when support for our releases end. Check the docs.
about.communityLedDesc: Feedback and contributors help decide what we do next.
about.getInvolvedDesc: Contribute code, get support, or just see what's going on.
about.codeAndPackagesDesc: Most of our code is on GitHub.
about.helpAndSupportDesc: Get help or talk to other users.
about.transparencyP1: We publish our code and contribute back where we can.
about.transparencyP2: We also publish support timelines on the documentation so you know when support ends.

help.title: Help & Support.
help.whatWeCanHelpWith: What we or our community can help with:
help.communityHubDesc: Join the Oreon community and get support in our community channels.

press.title: Press and Media.
press.subtitle: Media resources, press releases, and background info for journalists or content creators.
press.whatIsOreonP: Oreon is a desktop and laptop operating system designed for the user, the community, and the enterprise.
press.pressOutreachP: For interviews, detailed explanations, or any other inquiries, please contact our Founder, Brandon Lester by emailing him at blester@oreonhq.com.

legal.title: Legal
legal.subtitle: Privacy policy and other legal information for Oreon.
legal.yourDataIsYoursContent: Oreon HQ does not collect telemetry from end-user devices. Our commitment to privacy is absolute; your data remains on your hardware, under your control. We don't track your app usage, your web history, or your files.
legal.anonymizedMetricsContent: Starting with Oreon 10 and Oreon Lime (R2) (Build 2602) and later, download metrics are aggregate and anonymized. We monitor bandwidth allocation via Cloudflare for operational capacity planning only. No individual IP addresses are permanently stored or associated with specific downloads.
legal.useOfOreonContent: By downloading, installing, or using Oreon, you agree to these terms. Oreon is free and open source software. You may use it for any purpose (personal, educational, or commercial) without paying royalties or asking permission. You may share, modify, and redistribute Oreon in accordance with the licenses of the software it includes and the terms below.
legal.enterpriseOfferingsContent: Oreon HQ may offer specific components outside the Oreon OS for enterprise customers, including under separate commercial terms. Such offerings do not change the license or availability of the open source Oreon OS itself.
legal.openSourceThirdPartyContent: Oreon is built from free and open source components. Each component is distributed under its own license (such as the GPL, LGPL, MIT, and others). Your rights and obligations with respect to those components are governed by those licenses. Nothing in these terms restricts the rights granted to you by the applicable open source licenses. Where our own code is included, we license it under terms that are compatible with that ethos: you get the same freedoms to use, study, change, and share.
legal.noWarrantyContent: Oreon is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind, express or implied. This is standard for open source software: we do not guarantee that Oreon will be error-free, secure, or suitable for any particular use. You use it at your own risk. Some jurisdictions do not allow the exclusion of implied warranties, so these limitations may not fully apply to you.
legal.limitationOfLiabilityContent: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Oreon HQ and its contributors are not liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages arising from your use of Oreon (including loss of data, downtime, or business interruption). Our liability is limited to the fullest extent allowed under applicable law.
legal.trademarksContent: "Oreon" and the Oreon logo are trademarks of Oreon HQ. You may use the Oreon name and marks to refer to the software and to describe your use of it truthfully. You may not use our trademarks in a way that suggests endorsement, or to brand your own modified distribution, without permission. Independent projects and community efforts that clearly identify themselves as unofficial or community-run are generally fine when they do not mislead users.
legal.changesToTermsContent: We may update these terms from time to time. The current version will always be available on this page. Continued use of Oreon after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated terms. We do not use these terms to strip you of rights you already have under open source licenses.

oreon.heroSubtitle: Oreon 10 is a stable and easy to use desktop OS for people who want a more user friendly RHEL® alternative.
oreon.atAGlance1: Built on AlmaLinux 10, giving you an enterprise stable base with long-term support lasting until 2035.
oreon.atAGlance2: Uses a GNOME layout refined by us to feel familiar for users migrating from Windows or macOS, without the need for heavy customization. You can still customize it to your liking if you want to.
oreon.atAGlance3: Security lifecycle is planned from the release date starting December 12, 2024 through the 2035 EOS window for users who want to stay on the same OS for the full lifecycle. This means you can be sure that your system will be protected from security vulnerabilities for a long time.
oreon.whatOreon10Is1: Based on AlmaLinux 10 for a stable upstream base.
oreon.whatOreon10Is2: Uses a GNOME layout styled by us to reduce the learning curve for users coming from other operating systems.
oreon.whatOreon10Is3: Designed for daily usability first, not eye candy.
oreon.whatOreon10Is4: Security lifecycle runs from December 12, 2024 to the EOS date in 2035.
oreon.useCase1: You want a Linux desktop that does not need constant tweaking after install.
oreon.useCase2: You prefer a GNOME setup that feels cleaner and more familiar out of the box.
oreon.useCase3: You want a smaller, less-bloated default experience.
oreon.useCase4: You need a stable base for long-term systems where change matters.
oreon.getOreon10Desc: Download the latest build of Oreon 10. Give it a try and see if it's the right fit for you. You can try it from a live USB before installing!
